letters.desc: AEP notes that PJM has an active stakeholder process to develop large load interconnection reforms and urges the Commission to avoid disrupting that work with prescriptive federal requirements.
quotes: The Commission's reforms should avoid introducing additional delays to large load interconnection by disrupting state and regional-level efforts.

letters.desc: Antora cites the Commission's PJM Co-Location Order as recognizing the need for a permanent non-firm transmission service option, and argues temporary products like SPP CHILLS fail to meet that identified need.
quotes: CHILLS' temporary structure mirrors the Interim NITS product that the Commission required PJM to establish in its recent Co-Location Order, but does not fill the additional need the Commission identified in that proceeding, for the transmission provider to offer a permanent non-firm transmission service option.

letters.desc: Chevron notes PJM may propose an expedited interconnection process for paired large loads and generation and asks FERC to be open to it as an interim regional mechanism.
quotes: The Commission should be open to such regional fast-track proposals, which may provide mechanisms to connect large loads and generation before DOE ANOPR standards can be practicably established in all regions.

letters.desc: CEBA calls on FERC to expeditiously finish its ongoing PJM co-location technical review and clarify tariff rules across all markets to ensure reliability and fair cost allocation.
quotes: FERC should complete its review expeditiously and determine if PJM's tariff, as well as those of other electricity markets, need clearer rules to ensure grid reliability and fair allocation of costs.

letters.desc: Constellation directs most of its filing at PJM, where it has a pending complaint and the Show Cause record is fully developed. It documents Transmission Owner refusals to process studies, demands enforcement referral for non-compliant utilities, and requests a six-month study deadline and a replacement rate covering all viable co-location options.
quotes: the Commission should "build upon these principles" by issuing a full order in the PJM Show Cause proceedings consistent with the ANOPR's guidance based upon the extensive record already established in that consolidated docket.

The current load interconnection process in PJM in practice cedes control of all large load interconnections to the discretion of Transmission Owners, regardless of the facilities to which the load proposes to interconnect.

Some Transmission Owners have simply refused to participate in PJM's studies to analyze reliability impacts; and some, acting under unfiled interconnection study procedures, have changed their entire construct and timetable for processing load studies.

Some Transmission Owners have refused to allow new load connections unless the load agrees to the Transmission Owner's favored configuration or agrees to take other services offered by the Transmission Owner that the load does not need or wish to take and should not be required to take.

the Commission should issue a full order in the PJM Show Cause proceedings confirming its preliminary finding that the PJM Tariff is unjust and unreasonable because it does not contain "provisions addressing with sufficient clarity or consistency the rates, terms, and conditions of service that apply to co-location arrangements"

the Commission should also immediately issue an order in the PJM Show Cause proceedings ... adopting the Commission's preliminary finding that the PJM Tariff is unjust and unreasonable and establishing a replacement rate based on the record in those proceedings that reflects the ANOPR's guidance

the Commission should immediately order the following: PJM must establish a timeline -- with milestones -- for the completion of load interconnection studies for hybrid in-front-of-the-meter configurations ... with an absolute study completion deadline, including Transmission Owner input, of six months.

Transmission Owners will be subject to referral to the Commission's Office of Enforcement for any failure to diligently process large load interconnection requests or for conditioning the processing of such requests on the applicant's acceding to the Transmission Owner's favored configuration or unnecessary services

letters.desc: Constellation argues PJM already has a comprehensive, unrebutted record of Transmission Owner discrimination sufficient for a section 206 order this year. Multiple stalled hyperscale data center projects in PJM justify immediate region-specific relief separate from the broader rulemaking.
quotes: the Commission should issue an order on the merits in the PJM Show Cause proceedings and thereby: (i) take swift action to kickstart development on several stalled hyperscale data center projects in PJM; (ii) conclude, based on the comprehensive record in those proceedings, that the lack of clear rules allows the PJM Transmission Owners to unduly discriminate by still refusing to process large load behind-the-meter projects

In PJM, the Commission already has a comprehensive record, including substantial, unrebutted evidence of undue discrimination by PJM Transmission Owners against any behind-the-meter configuration, and any in front-of-the-meter configuration that avoids interconnection through the Transmission Owners' distribution facilities.

Some Transmission Owners have blocked behind-the-meter configurations and are extending that discrimination to front-of-the-meter connections to the grid (hybrid facilities), requiring that these facilities take distribution service or adopt configurations that would make net billing impossible.

the Commission should reject "Bring Your Own Generation" or "BYOG" proposals (such as PJM Option 6 in the Show Cause proceeding) that would allow state-favored resources to leapfrog the PJM queue, and should likewise reject proposals discussed in the ANOPR comments or in the IMM's recent complaint that would condition new large load interconnections (or expedited interconnection) upon the load bringing its own new generation.

No Transmission Owner can expedite service or study processing for projects taking the Transmission Owner's preferred type of service or configuration, or refuse to process a complete large load interconnection request on the ground that the large load has not 'arranged for wholesale transmission or retail distribution service.'

letters.desc: DCC specifically cites the pending PJM co-location proceeding (Docket Nos. EL25-49, EL25-20, AD24-11) as a ready record FERC should resolve quickly, then extend the resulting principles nationally.
quotes: DCC urged the Commission to act on the "complete record on co-location issues in PJM" to "deliver immediate clarity."

Resolving this issue in the existing dockets, and extending principles nationally through this rulemaking, is the most direct way to unlock the significant system benefits that hybrid configurations offer and to provide the certainty developers require.

letters.desc: EPSA repeatedly urges FERC to act on the pending PJM Show Cause proceeding, arguing that further delay is inconsistent with the ANOPR's intent to ensure timely and orderly large load interconnection.
quotes: It would be entirely inconsistent with the intent of the ANOPR to further delay resolution of the Show Cause proceeding to clarify the rules applicable to large load interconnections in PJM, which has been awaiting Commission action based on an extensive record for over six months.

letters.desc: esVolta cites PJM's load deliverability area approach as a model FERC should adopt nationally for defining which storage resources qualify for expedited large-load interconnection.
quotes: esVolta would go even further to support approaches in PJM that rightfully identify supply resources in the same "load deliverability area or LDA" as an eligible resource for the expedited interconnection process and similarly, in MISO, standalone storage and other resources that have agreements with large loads to provide needed resources and are located in the same "local resource zone or LRZ" should be deemed eligible for an expedited interconnection process completed within 90 days.

letters.org: Governor Josh Shapiro and Governor Glenn Youngkin
letters.desc: The governors reference the bipartisan PJM governors' LLA proposal pending before the PJM Board of Managers and frame their federal comments as consistent with that regional effort.
quotes: a more general solution to interconnection queue delays is critical to enable the important investments in manufacturing, AI, and infrastructure that are needed for the United States to compete and win.

letters.desc: Hopkins grounds her filing in PJM-specific data: the market monitor's attribution of 63% of the 833% capacity price increase to data centers, the resulting $9.3 billion spread across 67 million ratepayers in 13 states, and additional hidden transmission costs identified by the Union of Concerned Scientists. She calls for PJM's cost allocation to distinguish between infrastructure serving broad public load and infrastructure serving concentrated private commercial loads.
quotes: my electric bill is proof of the unfair and systematic transfer of costs from large commercial electricity consumers to residential ratepayers.
Penelec's residential Price to Compare has increased from 4.981 cents per kWh in March 2021 to 11.747 cents per kWh in December 2025.
The PJM independent market monitor has attributed 63% of the 833% capacity auction price increase between the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 delivery years to data center electricity demand.
This translates to $9.3 billion in costs being paid by 67 million ratepayers across the 13 PJM states.

The Union of Concerned Scientists identified an additional $4.3 billion in transmission interconnection costs previously obscured in utility filings, connecting private data centers directly to the high-voltage transmission system.
Any jobs, tax revenue, and economic activity created by those facilities remain in Virginia and Maryland, but the costs are socialized onto me and the other millions of ratepayers in PJM states.

require that PJM's capacity auction cost allocation methodology distinguish between infrastructure serving broad public load and infrastructure serving concentrated private commercial loads. The current framework treats these identically. They are not identical.
act before the Shapiro price cap expires in 2030. The cap has provided temporary protection for Pennsylvania ratepayers. Without action, costs will increase even more.

letters.desc: JCA focus their Expansion Rate Policy recommendation on PJM Supplemental Projects (Attachment M-3), noting these are intra-zonal, designed to meet specific customer needs, and less subject to RTEP-level regional scrutiny, making them the clearest and most urgent target for the new rate structure.
quotes: The JCA submit support for the Expansion Rate Policy as it applies at the local level for Supplemental Projects.

letters.desc: The VSCC points to PJM's failed Critical Issue Fast Path process as evidence that RTOs are not better positioned than states to resolve large load interconnection issues. It urges FERC to direct further PJM generation queue reform, including expansion of the Reliability Resource Initiative, as the most direct way to unblock load interconnections.
quotes: States are better equipped than the RTOs to address these matters efficiently. PJM recently conducted an 'expedited' process (the Critical Issue Fast Path process) to attempt to address large load addition issues, only to have its membership reject each of the dozen or so proposals.

the Commission should act within its existing jurisdiction to accelerate interconnection of generation needed to support load. As the Commission has noted in several PJM proceedings, the generation interconnection process desperately needs to be reformed.

The Commission should direct PJM to do more, including additional processes like the RRI. Removing the causes of generation interconnection backlogs would go far in accelerating load interconnections.

letters.desc: Vistra specifically calls out PJM-related pending proceedings, noting the Commission's inaction has created nationwide uncertainty and that unregulated PJM Transmission Owner processes are cost-allocating upgrades for large loads to the broader rate base without Commission oversight.
quotes: the Commission should begin by acting in the multiple long-pending dockets with well-developed evidentiary records.  Doing so would immediately resolve the regulatory uncertainty that has crippled the industry for the past 18 months.

Transmission owners that have unregulated generation affiliates or operate in states where large loads have the option to select a competitive supplier have a clear incentive to favor the interconnection of new large loads that agree to take electric service from their affiliated generation.  This incentive creates the potential for a textbook example of undue discrimination that must be remedied by a set of national rules that explicitly bar undue discrimination and with on-going compliance checks to ensure those rules are working as designed.

letters.desc: Eolian supports the PJM Co-Location Order as an important step but identifies two gaps: study models do not account for flexible load and generation arrangements, and non-firm services are limited to co-located loads rather than adjacent ones. The Matta Grid example shows how PJM's current process caused $158 million in study-assigned upgrade costs by omitting nearby load.
quotes: the Commission must require additional reforms beyond recently approved initiatives that some regions have enacted to ensure timely and affordable integration of large loads. While recent reforms in Southwest Power Pool (SPP) and PJM Interconnection, LLC (PJM) are positive steps, these reforms fall short of what is needed to fully address the large load interconnection challenges identified in the ANOPR.

PJM's Phase II study results assigned $158 million in network upgrade costs to Matta Grid, largely driven by a grid constraint 25 miles from both the Matta Grid project and the proposed Amazon data center. A Timmons Group study that Eolian commissioned demonstrated that, had PJM included even a very conservative 150 MW of the 770 MW of Amazon load in its Phase II study for Transition Cycle 1, the study results would have shown over $100 million less in system reinforcements assigned to the Matta Grid project.

Under PJM's current rules, however, there is little incentive for developers such as Eolian to locate assets to provide these system benefits. Developers do not get any credit or earn any additional revenues for opening additional system capacity.

letters.desc: Talen opposes giving PJM discretion to pick which loads interconnect or to prioritize BYOG, but supports modifying PJM's existing Reliability Backstop Auction and interconnection process as a market-based fix for resource adequacy.
quotes: Conditioning customer interconnections on BYOG or instructing PJM to deny service conflicts with bedrock open-access principles FERC established in Order No. 888 and Order No. 2000, which mandate non-discriminatory transmission service under a Commission-approved tariff.

Instructing PJM to pick winners and losers among loads would undermine the Commission’s open-access framework and invite litigation over undue discrimination, delaying urgently needed reliability solutions.
FERC should reject any proposal that allows PJM (or any other RTO/ISO) to deny interconnection or prioritize BYOG arrangements.

Talen suggests modifying the RBA so that the auction is triggered when the RPM auctions clear below 98% of the reserve margin requirement two base residual auctions in a row, rather than the current trigger of the base residual auctions clearing below 99% of the reserve margin three auctions in a row.
the Commission should direct PJM to develop a Reliability Resource Initiative-like interconnection process which will expedite the interconnection of all resources selected under the RBA mechanism.

letters.desc: The filer notes that only Dominion Energy among PJM transmission owners has significant DLR adoption planned, and that PJM Transmission Owners oppose ATT requirements. It argues Commission action is needed to overcome regional resistance.
quotes: we urge the Commission to encourage all RTOs to host forums to investigate the opportunity for ATTs and other solutions to increase capacity and improve affordability and how to integrate ATTs into all aspects of an RTO's processes.

letters.desc: Bloom uses PJM as the example of a region where current bifurcated study processes ignore co-located supply benefits and improperly identify required network upgrades.
quotes: under existing rules, load is studied as if it seeks firm rights to withdraw 100% from the transmission system to meet its requirements, while the generator is studied as if it seeks to inject 100% of its capacity into the transmission grid, with some RTOs, like PJM, requiring that generator capacity also be studied for deliverability to load throughout the system.  These bifurcated, non-integrated processes ignore on-site supply benefits and can improperly identify required Network Upgrades, resulting in slower interconnection and unnecessarily increasing Network Upgrade costs.

letters.desc: Buckeye specifically opposes AEP's proposal to spread data center transmission upgrade costs to all customers on a nationwide basis through an extra-high voltage postage stamp rate, noting it merely shifts costs rather than solving the underlying problem.
quotes: Buckeye opposes American Electric Power Service Corporation's ("AEP's") proposal to socialize data center transmission costs to other customers on a nationwide basis.

letters.desc: Senators highlight PJM capacity auction costs that have tripled and note that data centers will drive 90 percent of new demand over the next five years.
quotes: PJM's 2024 capacity market auction, which aims to secure resources to guarantee that the grid will be able to meet peak demand in the coming months, closed at a record high of $16.6 billion, up from just $2.2 billion in 2023.

In PJM Interconnection, the regional transmission organization (RTO) that serves thirteen states and the District of Columbia in the mid-Atlantic region, data centers will drive 90% of new power demand over the next five years.

letters.desc: Verrus disagrees with the PJM Independent Market Monitor's characterization of flexible data center loads as a regulatory fiction. Verrus argues the IMM's view reflects an outdated demand response conception and does not account for the physical infrastructure backing asset-backed flexible loads.
quotes: The Commission should require transmission providers to explicitly model flexible-load curtailment potential in their base-case and sensitivity analyses so that flexibility is valued in interconnection studies with respect to network upgrades, and in the studies that underlie local and regional transmission planning.

Verrus respects the long-standing role of the PJM Independent Market Monitor in safeguarding competitive markets, but disagrees with recent assertions that flexible data centers are a 'regulatory fiction.' That characterization reflects an older conception of demand response as voluntary or behavioral.

letters.desc: The VSCC points to PJM's existing generator interconnection queue as evidence that large regional queues create delays and unfairness across states. Giving PJM a large load queue would replicate these problems. PJM's Reliability Resource Initiative is cited positively as a fast-track model that could serve co-located resources without requiring a new RTO queue.
quotes: Develop a set of Commission-mandated minimum standards for large load interconnections, such as study deposits, site control requirements, and similar criteria while allowing transmission owners, and not the RTOs, who already face long delays and inefficiencies in their existing generation queues, to continue to manage large load interconnection queues with direct oversight of their state regulatory commissions.

the Commission should acknowledge the inefficiencies inherent to the large, regional queues administered by PJM and other RTOs. These inefficiencies can lead to longer queue lines and projects in states with available capacity being stuck behind projects in states that are already saturated.

The Commission should enable the accelerated interconnection of large loads that are willing to bring their own generation or to be co-located with generation by creating a fast-track generator interconnection queue for those verified generation resources, such as PJM's existing Commission-approved Reliability Resource Initiative.

letters.desc: AES flags that co-location and transmission charge questions are already before FERC in the PJM show cause proceeding and urges any new rules to account for that record to avoid inconsistent outcomes.
quotes: AES believes that the Commission could provide certainty to the market by issuing guidance, whether in the form of a policy statement or otherwise, regarding how termination fees from construction service agreements associated with transmission network upgrades should be accounted for in transmission rates.

letters.desc: Buckeye draws on PJM data to illustrate the scale of the problem: approximately $12 billion in transmission investment driven by data center load in the Dominion Zone alone, with costs currently socialized across all PJM customers rather than charged to the data centers that caused them.
quotes: Load growth of approximately 10,000 MW driven largely by data centers in the Dominion Zone of PJM resulted in approximately $12 billion in transmission investment across PJM.
While these costs are primarily driven by data center loads, currently all customers in the corresponding PJM transmission zones and, where applicable, in the broader PJM region will bear them.
Under AEP Ohio's retail tariff, these measures protect only AEP Ohio's own retail customers from these significant stranded transmission cost risks, leaving wholesale transmission customers exposed.

letters.desc: Buckeye draws on PJM-specific data throughout, citing $4.3 billion in 2024 local transmission proposals and over $24 billion in RTEP projects likely driven by data centers. The AEP Ohio and AES Ohio situations illustrate how existing state and bilateral mechanisms leave non-serving wholesale customers exposed.
quotes: Without action by the Commission, wholesale transmission customers like Buckeye, and the retail customers of its members, could be left shouldering billions in transmission costs.

FERC must have a role to address cost shifting among wholesale transmission customers within a TO's Zone and among various TO Zones. State commissions cannot address this issue because only the Commission has jurisdiction over transmission rates, such as those in PJM.

Although the Ohio Commission explicitly acknowledged concerns about cost shifts to other wholesale transmission customers, it declined to take any action to address them. Instead, it found that these issues 'are statutorily outside of [the PUCO's] intrastate purview.'
Data centers have likely caused over $24 billion in RTEP projects so far.

letters.desc: The Center cites PJM's $5.1 billion transmission buildout for Virginia data centers as a concrete example of how cost allocation rules leave Maryland residential ratepayers covering two-thirds of their state's share for infrastructure that serves data centers in another state.
quotes: PJM spent $5.1 billion on new transmission, and half of those costs were distributed to member utilities based on their share of power demand... in Maryland for example, residential ratepayers will then pay for two-thirds of the state's overall share in transmission costs, even though PJM is building this new transmission for Virginia data centers and not the average Maryland residential ratepayer.

letters.desc: EEI notes that PJM has an ongoing stakeholder process producing promising proposals for large load interconnection and urges that a final federal rule not undermine those regional efforts.
quotes: the Commission should ensure that any national procedures do not undermine the RTO and utility-specific processes.

letters.desc: EEI notes FERC's order directing PJM to establish transparent co-location rules as evidence of existing regional progress to build upon.
quotes: Commission orders across several regions that: Direct PJM to establish transparent rules to facilitate service of AI-driven data centers and other large loads co-located with generating facilities.

letters.desc: EPSA references the PJM show cause proceeding as the foundation for near-term co-located load guidance, citing its extensive record developed over more than nine months.
quotes: EPSA urges the Commission to move forward with direction and guidance for co-located arrangements based on the extensive record set out in the PJM Show Cause proceeding on these issues.

letters.desc: ECA notes PJM has struggled to define pathways for large load customers partly due to jurisdictional uncertainty and absent Commission guidance. PJM capacity prices have risen over 800% across the last three auctions while a clear integration plan remains lacking.
quotes: regions like PJM Interconnection, L.L.C. (PJM) and Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (SPP) have faced challenges in addressing large load growth and defining pathways for large load customers to obtain service while protecting other customers from reliability and cost risks, owing in part to jurisdictional uncertainties and a lack of guidance from the Commission on key implementation issues.

letters.desc: Emerald AI cites PJM as an example of a congested region where workload migration to a less constrained area such as MISO can act as a virtual transmission line, relieving local constraints without new infrastructure.
quotes: If the PJM interconnection is thermally constrained but the MISO region has excess wind generation, an orchestrator can route new inference requests to the MISO facility, for example. This capability acts as a "virtual transmission line." Instead of moving megawatts of electrons across a congested wire to meet a static demand, the system moves the demand for those electrons to a location where power is abundant.

letters.desc: ETI cites recent PJM events, including over $400 million in 2025 uplift costs from a January winter storm and post-settlement penalty reductions from Winter Storm Elliott, as evidence that PJM market design undermines investment signals.
quotes: price suppressing events remain a persistent problem in these markets––even as recently as with the PJM uplift that arose out of the January 2025 winter storm in the Northeast––thus undermining the signals that the prices should convey.

[R]ecent extreme winter weather has once again highlighted critical flaws in PJM's market structure, resulting in over $400 million in uplift costs in 2025 year-to-date—expenses that cannot be hedged by load-serving entities through forward energy purchases and which are often passed directly to consumers.
Such after-the-fact adjustments make it difficult for investors to assess the potential viability of electricity projects.

letters.desc: Entergy takes no position on PJM-specific claims but cautions that problems documented for PJM or individual transmission owners there cannot be extrapolated to other regions.
quotes: the Commission cannot automatically extrapolate specific claims made about load interconnections in one area to other parts of the country

letters.desc: ELPC cites PJM as the region where the socialization of large-load connection costs is most documented, with $4.1 billion in such costs in 2024 alone and the trend worsening into 2025 and beyond.
quotes: Mr. Jacobs provided his analysis showing that such connection facilities added up to $4.1 billion across PJM in 2024 alone, with costs continuing to increase in 2025 and beyond.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy operates in PJM and cites PJM's proposed expedited large-load interconnection track as a model for Commission reform. Its threshold and queue recommendations align with PJM-specific conditions.
quotes: the Commission should limit any rule to (1) data centers that (2) have loads of at least 200 MW.

The Commission should consider reforms in this proceeding that allow interconnection-ready projects to timely advance through the queue, similar to PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.'s ("PJM") consideration of rules for an expedited interconnection track for the interconnection of data centers and other large loads.

letters.desc: FirstEnergy notes that large load interconnections requiring regional upgrades are already reviewed through PJM's Regional Transmission Expansion Plan process, undercutting the case for new federal competition mandates.
quotes: The Commission should not require that all network upgrades that are determined to be necessary solutions to interconnecting large load customers be included as projects subject to competition in regional transmission planning processes.

letters.desc: Google cites Princeton ZERO Lab research showing that a flexible grid connection combined with a bring-your-own-capacity framework in PJM could cut interconnection wait times by three to five years with minimal curtailment burden.
quotes: combining flexible grid connections with a "bring-your-own-capacity" framework in PJM could shorten interconnection wait times by three to five years and maintain grid power availability for over 99% of hours, while requiring on-site resource dispatch for only 40 to 70 hours annually.

letters.desc: GridCARE notes PJM's Critical Issue Fast Path as an existing regional example of streamlined study processes that incorporate flexibility and behavioral data.
quotes: PJM's Critical Issue Fast Path, SPP's High-Impact Large Load process, and ISO-NE's ongoing work on load characterization all demonstrate that regions are exploring ways to streamline studies, incorporate temporal and behavioral data, better align study processes with actual system operations, and improve coordination with utilities.

letters.desc: The filing documents PJM capacity price increases of 833% and 1,038% over consecutive auction years, and notes the ComEd large-load interconnection queue has grown from 80 MW in 2019 to 8,272 MW in 2025, exceeding ComEd's all-time system peak.
quotes: In PJM capacity prices effective June 1, 2025 skyrocketed by approximately 833% increasing from $28.92 per MW-day to $269.92 per MW-day, and further increased to $329.17 per MW-day for 2026-2027.
large load interconnection requests accounted for only 80 MW in 2019, but jumped to 652 MW in 2022, to 3,931 MW in 2024, and to an astonishing 8,272 MW in 2025.

large load projects create significant risks, including the risks of: (1) insufficient supply to meet existing demand and the additional demand of large load projects, (2) skyrocketing prices both in response to insufficient supply and to provide "incentives" in the hope that increased generator revenues will cause them to build sufficient generation to meet the large load demand, and (3) electricity shortages leading to blackouts or "load shed."

letters.desc: The filer references PJM as carrying a substantial share of the national interconnection backlog that exceeded 2,000 gigawatts by 2024, and identifies PJM as one of the RTOs that should file tariff amendments for node-level demand caps. The region is cited as evidence of systemic queue dysfunction rather than as a primary reform target.
quotes: The interconnection queue, which nationally had grown to over two thousand gigawatts of pending requests by 2024, with PJM accounting for a substantial share of that backlog, functions on a first-come, first-served allocation mechanism that rewards queue position rather than siting quality.

PJM, MISO, SPP, and other RTOs and ISOs operating under FERC jurisdiction should file tariff amendments implementing node-level demand caps for large-load interconnection. Caps should be set at the fault-level capacity available at each interconnection point, net of existing committed load.

letters.desc: IECA identifies PJM as the primary region experiencing significant large load interconnection delays, citing the DCC BYOG Pathway as an example of a targeted cross-jurisdictional remedy being developed there.
quotes: In the grid administered by the PJM Interconnection LLC ("PJM"), for example, interconnections of large loads are experiencing significant delays.

letters.desc: IECA notes that the EL25-49 show-cause proceeding has produced a substantial record on PJM co-location issues and asks FERC to use that record when crafting ANOPR guidance on transmission protections.
quotes: the Commission and its Staff should now have a relatively complete record on "co-location" issues in PJM on which to formulate and propose guidance in response to the ANOPR regarding the range of acceptable transmission system protection provisions that counterparties could apply to co-location arrangements involving large loads and co-located generation resources located at the same point of interconnection or at "proximate" points of interconnection with the interstate transmission grid.

letters.desc: LS Power references PJM's Necessary Study process as an example of an appropriate limited reliability assessment for co-located or hybrid arrangements, distinct from the broader SSR/RMR-type analysis the ANOPR proposes.
quotes: Large-load interconnection should be integrated into existing planning and study processes for generation interconnection. Large-load integration should be handled within the same coordinated regional planning and study framework used for generation and reliability.

letters.desc: Maryland describes PJM processes for large load adjustment and notes that interconnection queue delays have raised consumer costs in recent capacity auctions. The state urges that expedited large load studies preserve the efficiency of PJM's generator queue.
quotes: MEA urges that any expediting of interconnection studies of large loads ensure minimal disruption to PJM's generation interconnection process
Interconnection bottlenecks impart real costs for Maryland consumers

letters.desc: The Maryland PSC cites PJM IMM analysis showing large capacity and energy price increases from removing nuclear generation as a proxy for large load additions, and notes the 2026/2027 BRA cleared below the RTO Reliability Requirement, underscoring the tight supply outlook.
quotes: According to the IMM, removing 10,000 MW of nuclear generation in the entire PJM footprint would have increased capacity prices in the state of Maryland by approximately 47% ($526 million) relative to the 2025/2026 Base Residual Auction ("BRA") results.

Existing generation currently serving customers should not be allowed to suspend their existing service, in whole or in part, simply to serve new large load. Such a suspension would have an adverse impact on cost and raise energy prices.

letters.desc: The filer references PJM specifically to illustrate the scale of ratepayer-funded data centre upgrades (over $4.3 billion in 2024 in PJM-footprint states) and industry opposition to mandatory flexible connections, as well as PJM's analysis of co-location options.
quotes: both Data Centres and Supplier companies in the USA have opposed a proposed imposition of flexible connections by the PJM citing legality, fairness and grid reliability.

customers from Illinois, Maryland, New Jersey, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Virginia and West Virginia, collectively paid over US$ 4.3 billion in 2024 for grid investments that were only necessary to accommodate new data centres.
However, the American network operator, PJM, reveals several complications in its May 2025 publication, showing 8 options for large load co-location, identifying unique grid impacts of each.

letters.desc: MISO notes that large load growth could worsen congestion on the MISO-PJM seam and affect the Market-to-Market coordination process if a uniform interconnection rule does not also address cross-border flow management.
quotes: if the Commission decides to move forward with standard large load interconnection procedures, it should also consider how to mitigate the potential increase in congestion along the seam(s) that could result from the interconnection of large loads.

letters.desc: The filing focuses exclusively on PJM, documenting that data center growth has already driven an 82 percent increase in capacity auction revenues and is the primary cause of tight supply conditions. The Monitor filed a companion formal complaint against PJM alongside this ANOPR comment.
quotes: PJM is currently proposing to allow the interconnection of large new data center loads that it cannot serve reliably and that will require load curtailments (black outs) of the data centers or of other customers at times.

The Market Monitor requests that the Commission rule that PJM has the authority to add large new data center loads only when they can be served reliably as defined both by transmission and capacity adequacy.
Data center load growth is the primary reason for recent and expected capacity market conditions, including total forecast load growth, the tight supply and demand balance, and high prices.

inclusion of existing and forecast data center load in the peak load forecast for 2026 resulted in a $7,271,197,971 or an 82.1 percent increase in capacity market revenues for the 2026/2027 RPM Base Residual Auction.
The Market Monitor believes that under current rules, PJM does have the authority to require that the loads can be served reliably before allowing the loads to be added to the system.
PJM has the authority to create a load queue.
None of the proposals have addressed the fact that PJM does not have the authority or the capability to order or enforce curtailments.

more explicit rules are plainly needed in order to remove confusion and to provide PJM the tools to protect resource adequacy and to ensure just and reasonable capacity prices and to ensure that there is a clear path to provide for the reliable interconnection of large new data center loads.
The market solution is to require new large data center loads to bring their own new generation with locational and temporal characteristics matched to their load profile.
If large new data center loads want an expedited interconnection process, loads should be required to bring their own new generation.
It is not unduly discriminatory to identify the class of large data centers and impose requirements on that class that match the impact of that class on all other customers.
In their current and proposed forms, demand side solutions offer no viable substitution for generation capacity resources.

It is not an overstatement to assert that the ongoing addition of large data center loads will put PJM competitive markets at risk unless there is a solution that requires large data center loads to pay for the costs that they would otherwise impose on other customers.

All of the currently identified options require PJM to plan the transmission system to meet large data center loads consistent with the RTEP and require all customers to pay an allocated share of the transmission upgrades required to serve large data center load additions.

letters.desc: The filing is explicitly scoped to PJM, where the Market Monitor identifies an immediate and urgent shortage of generation capacity relative to projected data center load growth of approximately 30,000 MW. PJM's existing market structure and lack of load queue authority make federal action urgent.
quotes: Commenters with specific proposals generally seek to avoid the only just, reasonable and not unduly discriminatory action available to the Commission that will protect reliability and affordability for existing customers which is to provide clear incentives to large new data center loads to get to market quickly and reliably and to refuse to permit reliability to be undermined by adding large new data center loads without corresponding new generation.

The ANOPR does not propose to include a requirement in the interconnection procedures for large loads, that interconnection of large loads to the grid must be predicated on the ability to provide reliable service which in turn requires generation capacity which in turn means that there should be a load queue. The NOPR should include such a requirement.

The best incentive to bring only real projects is to provide an expedited option to bring your own new generation. This incentive would be much stronger and more effective and more focused on a real solution than requiring deposits.

There is no reason to simply extend the generator threshold to loads. Generators have generally been very large compared to individual loads. While there is no completely objective threshold for large new data center loads, the threshold should be no higher than five MW.
The suggestion that the cutoff for the load queue should be 200 MW is an attempt to avoid the issue, would miss many data centers and would permit gaming of the rules to avoid the queue.

The Market Monitor's view is that there is a market based path forward to reliably serving large new data center loads that does not require a change in jurisdictional authorities or a lengthy and contentious debate about jurisdiction.
State regulators cannot protect retail customers from the impact of adding large new data center loads on PJM wholesale market prices for capacity, energy and reserves and on system reliability.

Co-located load is simply a way to wish away the reliability issue and more importantly to undermine the PJM markets and impose unacceptably large reliability and monetary costs on all other PJM customers.

The Commission should reject the co-location option as inconsistent with PJM's competitive markets, inconsistent with just and reasonable rates, and inconsistent with the goal of the ANOPR to ensure the timely and orderly interconnection of large loads.
In their current and proposed forms, demand side solutions offer no viable substitution for generation capacity resources.

If 20,000 MW of new data center load were added and 90 percent or less of this load were offered in the capacity market as emergency demand side resources, the Market Monitor estimates that the increased cost of capacity would be around $5.48 billion per year to existing customers.

The narrowly defined co-location model that is the subject of Constellation's Complaint and Constellation's ongoing comments in the PJM CIFP process would allow existing generation to sell to a large new data center load and withdraw from the PJM capacity market. If allowed, this option could lead to the end of PJM markets.

The Market Monitor agrees with PJM's points and thinks that PJM understates the negative outcomes of connect and manage. Ignoring the issues at the time of interconnection and imposing the actual costs as they are realized on other customers is not consistent with the stated purpose of the ANOPR.

All customers should be full NITS customers and pay their full share of transmission costs without calculations of asserted gross impacts, net impacts or other attempts to avoid paying for transmission service.

quotes: the reforms in this docket should apply to new loads greater than 20 MW. This threshold is likely too small to make interconnection processes meaningfully more efficient and may overtake state-level proceedings where voltage thresholds have been set higher than this threshold. letters.org: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer AdvocateDelaware Division of the Public Advocate
letters.desc: The filers situate their comments in PJM's current resource adequacy and affordability crisis, where 30 GW of projected peak load growth through 2030 comes from data centers and capacity prices have risen more than tenfold, underscoring the urgency of protective requirements.
quotes: The Joint Consumer Advocates support establishing a large load and hybrid interconnection queue that is centrally managed by the same entity that manages/administers resource adequacy processes, like PJM. This queue should have standardized study deposits, readiness requirements, and withdrawal penalties to deter speculative projects and provide transmission providers and RTOs with useful information to forecast demand on their systems accurately.

letters.desc: PJM provides concrete data from its own operations: stability studies take about 6 months, a 60-day mandate is not feasible, and standing up any new large load process would require at least 12 months after a final rule.
quotes: Can any large load interconnection studies – expedited or otherwise – be completed in 60 days?  Based on PJM's experience in managing, coordinating, and performing interconnection studies under the best of circumstances, such a timeline is not likely to be feasible in reality at least in the shorter-term horizon though PJM is certainly committed to acting with as much speed and accuracy as possible consistent with Good Utility Practice.

Today, it takes approximately 6 months to complete stability studies due to the complexity of the data, modeling, and analytical processes.  And any additional expedited processes – serial in nature or otherwise – may exacerbate or reintroduce queue backlogs for generator interconnection projects subject to cluster studies.

PJM anticipates needing at least 12 or more additional months to implement any new large load interconnection process (although this estimate is admittedly speculative since the full details of the proposed reforms are not yet clearly known).

Many of these principles could be addressed through the existing PJM necessary study process that PJM previously utilized to study, develop, and modify existing generator interconnections and agreements seeking to co-locate large loads.  This effectively means no FERC action may be needed to accomplish some of the proposed reforms in certain instances.

letters.desc: PPL Electric operates in PJM territory and reports that its Pennsylvania interconnection process has not delayed any data center project, with over 20 GW in advanced development stages and 5 GW under active construction.
quotes: Pennsylvania's efficient oversight has not added a single day to any data center development timeline. Each site is proceeding as quickly as possible given broader issues such as land acquisition/permitting and global supply chains for necessary components.

letters.desc: The filing specifically highlights PJM ratepayers as having faced outsized impacts from the rapid proliferation of data centers, and notes that 3,844 Sierra Club members in the PJM footprint signed letters urging action.
quotes: The rapid proliferation of data centers has already caused significant harms to existing ratepayers across the country.
Ratepayers in PJM, however, have seen an outsized impact.
